periods.analysis: Harborview is starting this cycle from a strong trust position: Community Events Held came in at 9, which is 3 above the >=6 target, and Neighborhood Watch Groups Active stood at 34, 4 above the >=30 target. With no prior quarter in this series for comparison, I am treating 2024-Q3 as the operating baseline for this objective. The strongest lift came from the summer Harborfront Safety Nights, the Back-to-School crosswalk tables, and Sector 2 captain walk-throughs along Bayview, Mariner, and East Cliff routes. The result is green, and the important point is procedural: visibility was scheduled, documented, and distributed across neighborhoods rather than concentrated in one high-profile event.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the 9-event quarterly planning template and lock dates at least 45 days out through the Community Policing calendar. Extend the Sector 2 captain walk-through model to Sectors 4 and 5, with attendance logs and issue-resolution notes entered into the trust dashboard within five business days. Keep the Neighborhood Watch captain roster current by confirming alternates for all 34 active groups before the next quarterly review.

periods.analysis: Performance remained green in 2024-Q4, with Community Events Held at 7, down 2 from 9 in 2024-Q3 but still 1 above the >=6 target. Neighborhood Watch Groups Active was 33, down 1 from 34 and still 3 above the >=30 target. The seasonal reduction was expected as outdoor evening events tapered after October, while the department shifted to holiday retail foot patrol briefings at Harborview Commons and the North Pier shopping corridor. I do not see an engagement failure here; I see a normal seasonal compression that was managed without dropping below standard.
periods.recommendations: Preserve the winter minimum of 7 events by pairing smaller roll-call meetups with scheduled community rooms at libraries, schools, and senior centers. Reconfirm the one inactive or drifting watch group from the Q3 roster and assign a community service officer to complete a captain check-in by mid-January. Continue publishing post-event summaries so residents can see which concerns were logged and which unit owns follow-up.

periods.analysis: The green trend held in 2025-Q1: Community Events Held rose to 9, up 2 from 7 in 2024-Q4 and 3 above the >=6 target. Neighborhood Watch Groups Active moved to 31, down 2 from 33 but still 1 above the >=30 target. The event recovery reflects good execution on the winter indoor strategy, especially the Civic Center listening sessions and the youth safety cohort meetings with Harborview High, Pelican Ridge, and Southshore Middle. The watch-group decline is small but worth watching, because trust systems depend on continuity, not just event volume.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 9-event cadence, but require every event packet to include a named follow-up owner and a 30-day closure check. For the 31 active watch groups, prioritize retention by contacting the two groups lost since 2024-Q4 and offering a combined captain refresher at Fire Station 6. Add a simple watch-item to the dashboard: groups without a documented captain contact in the last 60 days.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q2 strengthened the position, with Community Events Held at 11, up 2 from 9 in 2025-Q1 and 5 above the >=6 target. Neighborhood Watch Groups Active increased to 33, up 2 from 31 and 3 above the >=30 target. This was not accidental; the Safe Summer Launch, marina outreach tables, and apartment-community meetings on the Route 14 and Route 22 corridors created multiple points of contact before peak visitor season. The objective remains green, and the quarter shows that disciplined outreach can rebuild watch participation without relying on one-time publicity.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Safe Summer Launch as a standing Q2 program and assign one lieutenant to track commitments made at each of the 11 events. Convert the two reactivated watch groups into stable participants by giving them captain kits, block-map templates, and direct non-emergency liaison contacts. Use Q2 attendance data to identify the three highest-yield venues and reserve them now for the next annual cycle.

periods.analysis: The objective stayed green in 2025-Q3, with Community Events Held at 9, down 2 from 11 in 2025-Q2 but still 3 above the >=6 target. Neighborhood Watch Groups Active reached 35, up 2 from 33 and 5 above the >=30 target. The event count normalized after the heavy Q2 summer launch, while watch participation improved through the Harborfront condo captain cohort and the Westgate neighborhood canvass. That tradeoff is acceptable: fewer events than Q2, but deeper resident structure and broader coverage.
periods.recommendations: Sustain at least 9 events in Q3 by keeping National Night Out, Harbor Days, and the school-opening safety route briefings on the core calendar. Protect the gain to 35 active watch groups by assigning quarterly check-ins to the community policing sergeants by sector. Begin testing a shared incident-prevention bulletin for watch captains, with clear language on what to report, how to report it, and what not to escalate.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q4 remained green, with Community Events Held at 7, down 2 from 9 in 2025-Q3 and still 1 above the >=6 target. Neighborhood Watch Groups Active was 34, down 1 from 35 and 4 above the >=30 target. The same seasonal pattern appeared as last year, but the floor is holding because precinct open houses, holiday fraud briefings, and downtown merchant walks were scheduled before the calendar compressed. I am comfortable with the result, provided we do not let the modest watch-group dip become a first-quarter slide.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the 7-event winter floor and pre-book indoor venues before Thanksgiving each year. Contact the one group that fell off the active list and document whether the issue is captain turnover, meeting fatigue, or boundary overlap with a neighboring group. Carry the holiday fraud briefing materials into January utility-bill and online-scam sessions for seniors and small businesses.

periods.analysis: In 2026-Q1, performance stayed green as Community Events Held returned to 9, up 2 from 7 in 2025-Q4 and 3 above the >=6 target. Neighborhood Watch Groups Active declined to 32, down 2 from 34 but still 2 above the >=30 target. The department executed the indoor engagement playbook well, including the North Harbor tenant meetings, youth diversion roundtables, and the quarterly faith-leader briefing. The watch-group movement is the only item I would mark for close attention, because two straight winter-to-spring roster losses could weaken the resident reporting chain if left unattended.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the rebound to 9 events and add a captain-recruitment table to every Q1 community meeting. Direct community policing staff to complete a 32-group roster audit, including captain name, alternate, preferred contact method, and last meeting date. Set a recovery target of at least two reactivated groups by the end of Q2 through apartment-manager outreach and neighborhood association partnerships.

periods.analysis: 2026-Q2 closes the arc in a strong green position: Community Events Held increased to 11, up 2 from 9 in 2026-Q1 and 5 above the >=6 target. Neighborhood Watch Groups Active improved to 34, up 2 from 32 and 4 above the >=30 target. The Q1 watch concern was addressed through the captain audit, the East Cliff apartment-manager cohort, and patrol-led bike-safety pop-ups along the Shoreline Trail. This is the kind of trust performance Harborview needs as it grows: repeatable, measured, and visible in the places residents actually use.
periods.recommendations: Institutionalize the Q2 model by making the captain audit, apartment-manager cohort, and Safe Summer outreach a single annual operating package. Keep the 11-event capacity only if each event has documented attendance, issues raised, and closure status; volume without follow-through does not protect trust. Use the restored 34 active watch groups to pilot a quarterly two-way briefing, with residents receiving trend data and the department receiving location-specific concerns before deployment plans are finalized.

periods.analysis: Nine events and 35 active watch groups both exceed their respective targets. Events declined from the spring peak, so maintaining follow-through matters more than increasing the count alone.
periods.recommendations: Review unresolved event concerns with patrol liaisons and keep the watch-group roster current.
